name: bending-gallery

frames.best_why: Frame 2 shows four captioned photo cards laid along the clearest visible arc.

tagline: Photo cards ride a curved arc and slide sideways as you drag.
summary: A band of rounded photo cards with short captions, arranged on a shallow arc where outer cards dip and lean away. Dragging or swiping slides them endlessly while the pictures ripple gently.
appearance: A wide strip of portrait photo cards runs across a black stage, each with a small white caption underneath. The row bows so cards near the middle sit higher and cards at the edges drop and tilt, with cards running off both sides.
behaviour: Dragging or swiping shifts the whole row, easing to a stop on a card boundary and looping cards that leave one edge back in at the other. Each photo also sways a little in place, and the strip re-fits when the window resizes.
demo_content: Nature photos captioned Single Leaf, Alpine Sunrise, Rice Terraces, Icelandic Horses, Autumn Canopy and Blue Lotus.
search_phrases: webgl image gallery you can drag
showcase of nature photos with captions
use_when: A portfolio or product page needs an immersive drag-through gallery of captioned photos.
avoid_when: It draws in WebGL only, so without WebGL the box stays empty, and images must allow cross-origin loading.
customise: items supplies image and caption pairs; bend, textColor, borderRadius and font are props, while camera, easing and shader sway are in the source.
weight_why: A WebGL draw call every frame for every card, plus a Canvas2D label texture for each.

a11y.note: Everything including captions is painted into a canvas, with no alt text or keyboard control and no reduced-motion check.

issues: Wheel, mousedown and touch listeners sit on the whole window, so the gallery hijacks page scrolling.
Captions are baked into textures, so they cannot be selected, translated or read by assistive tech.
polish_why: Smooth curved scroll with crisp photos and neat captions; edge cards clip awkwardly.
title: Bending Gallery
